title: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (September 2026)
source: EST: PRIMARY-STATED BY OPEC ITSELF, still filed estimate on prefix grounds. OPEC's August 2026 Monthly Oil Market Report (cover date 12 August 2026) prints verbatim "Next report to be issued on 10 September 2026" — read 2026-09-06 from the primary PDF on opec.org's own asset host, www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/momr-august-2026.pdf and siblings, which serve HTTP 200 while every opec.org HTML page, publications.opec.org/momr and momr.opec.org all return 403. Nineteen consecutive editions were pulled and chained: each report's "next report" line equals the following report's cover date, 18/18 (2025: Jan 15, Feb 12, Mar 12, Apr 14, May 14, Jun 16, Jul 15, Aug 12, Sep 11, Oct 13, Nov 12, Dec 11; 2026: Jan 14, Feb 11, Mar 11, Apr 13, May 13, Jun 11, Jul 13, Aug 12). The originating investing.com row matches that primary history 9/9 on dates, but its stated TIME (10:00 London = 09:00 UTC) is falsified — the PDFs' embedded creation stamps run 07:03-11:23 UTC with 11 of 19 at or after 10:00 UTC, and all 19 precede the 12:00 UTC that Reuters quotes OPEC as emailing, so the release lands nearer 08:00 ET than 05:00 ET. Stays estimate for two reasons that have nothing to do with date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no OPEC: confirmed prefix, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in its own sweep. Discovered during the iea-omr-2026-09-11 initial research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06); primary-verified during the opec-momr-2026-09-10 initial research. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The producer cartel's own number, and the middle leg of an agency triple this calendar tracked only one third of: EIA STEO 2026-09-09, OPEC MOMR 2026-09-10, IEA OMR 2026-09-11 — three forecasting agencies publishing on three consecutive sessions. Its research value is the question the iea-omr-2026-09-11 research left open: the two consumer-side agencies disagree by 51% on the same month's Gulf shut-in (EIA ~5.5 mb/d vs IEA 8.3 mb/d for July 2026), so no single supply figure is currently a fact and the producer side's read is the one independent number nobody has looked at. Filed low on the same reasoning as eia-steo-2026-09-09 and iea-omr-2026-09-11: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape, and the OMR base rate measured on 2026-09-06 (0 of 13 releases beating the ordinary same-hour p95 on either crude benchmark) is the closest available prior for what a monthly oil report does to the tape. It also lands on an already-thick session — PPI, the ECB decision, the 30Y bond auction, the 10y20y buyback operation and a coupon announcement all print 2026-09-10 — so treat it as a data source to read after the fact, never as a scheduled catalyst. ANSWERED 2026-09-06 by docs/research/events/opec-momr-2026-09-10.md: OPEC publishes no shut-in metric at all, but recomputing its August-edition Table 5-7 against the pre-war 4Q25 quarter puts July 2026 Middle East DoC production 5.20 mb/d below pre-war (5.72 among the countries that fell) — within 0.3 of the EIA and 3.1 below the IEA, so the producer corroborates the EIA and the pair becomes a trio, two-to-one. A MOMR-specific base rate was measured the same session across 20 primary-dated releases: 0 of 20 beat Brent's own-hour p95 (and 0 of 20 its p90) in the 12:00-13:00 UTC release bar, max move 1.011%.
